__meta.title: Live Defense — sourced KEV exploitation evidence per ATT&CK technique
sources: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (CC0 1.0; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md section 1.5)
__meta.method: Each KEV CVE is mapped to ATT&CK technique(s) by the exploitation nature of its CWE (high-confidence anchor only; the low-confidence CWE->CAPEC->ATT&CK fan-out is not used). Heat = sum of recency(0.5^(age/half-life)) x severity (known ransomware use adds 50%), measured from the snapshot date. A KEV CVE whose weakness anchors no technique does not heat.
__meta.note: Keyed by techniqueID. Each entry is the evidence behind that cell's heat: a cite-or-abstain brief and the KEV CVEs that map to it (newest/heaviest first, capped; itemCount is exact). A technique absent here does not heat (fail quiet). Absence is not evidence of safety.

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.brief: 1215 KEV CVEs in the CISA KEV snapshot map to this technique by the exploitation weakness (CWE) of each. That is the highest KEV exploitation pressure of any technique. 249 are KEV-linked to known ransomware campaign use. The most recent was added 2026-10-16. Heat is recency-weighted with a 180-day half-life, as of the 2026-10-16 KEV snapshot; it reflects KEV exploitation pressure, not your defensive posture.
